Each item has the Today item's shape: kind request, requestId, title, dueDate, overdue, priority, statusId and record (the request).

service.description: The intake settings of a project (workEffortId), or of an organization for requests with no project (organizationPartyId): the project's own WorkEffortSettings, else the organization's PartySettings ProjIntake (triagePartyId, defaultType, offered, triaged) and ProjPublicForm (captcha, files, maxMb, maxFiles, confirm), with the defaults filled in. settings: accountId and plusTag (the mail that files into the project), token (the public form's, empty when it is off), triagePartyId, defaultType, offeredTypes and triagedTypes (lists of RequestType ids; triaged: the types Projects triages with no project), requestFromWork (Y or N), and publicForm {captcha, files, maxMb, maxFiles, confirm}.
Turns on a project's public request form, or rotates its link: a new random token (WstIntakeToken), so the old link stops working. The form is at /r/<token> (IronStone's token route r).
Turns off a project's public request form: its link stops working.
Internal: the project whose public form token this is (a WstIntakeToken of an open project), or none. A malformed token is not looked up.

The token check of the public request form's token-route (/r/<token>; the framework calls it with token and routeName before anything of the page runs). A token that is not a project's open form is not valid, so the route answers its "not found" page. routeContext has what the form shows and nothing internal: projectName, the request types offered ({enumId, label}), whether files are taken and their limits, and the CAPTCHA's site key when the CAPTCHA is on. Read only; the submit checks the token again.

A request from a project's public form (/r/<token>), for a visitor who is not signed in: the token picks the project (an unknown, rotated or turned-off one is refused as "not available", nothing else said). Every field is checked: first and last name and email (an address), a subject (at most 255 characters) and a description (at most 20000), a type the project offers, an organization (kept as a note), at most maxFiles files of at most maxMb each, of the kinds a request may hold (pictures, PDF, text, office documents and archives; never html, svg or scripts), their names cleaned. A filled honeypot field (website) is taken as a robot: answered as received, nothing made. Too many requests from the form of the project in the last hour (30), or from the same address (5), are refused for now. With the CAPTCHA on, the token from the visitor's browser is verified (create#ContactRequestReCaptcha). The requester is found by email and first name, or made (create#ContactRequest: Reporter and Customer); the request is Submitted in the project on channel Web (ScWeb), its files are RequestContent, the triage assignee is its Assignee. The confirmation goes from the project's intake account when it has one and the form sends one. The answer is only the request's id.

service.description: The createRequest action of the mail client's rules (org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.run#EmailRules, through the EmailRuleAction enumeration ErActCreateRequest): a received message becomes a request, or joins one. - A message already on a request is left (running the rules again makes nothing twice). - A reply in a request's thread (its In-Reply-To or References name a message on the request, or its thread's first message is on it) joins that request's conversation and makes nothing new. - Else a Submitted request on channel email (ScEmail): the project the action's value names, else the project whose plus tag the message was sent to (an address with +tag), else none (a request to triage with no project). A project is taken only when its intake account (WstIntakeAccount) is the message's account, or the rule's owner (ruleOwnerUserId) is one of its parties; otherwise the request has no project. The type is the project's default, the subject its name, the text its description; the sender is the Reporter and Customer (a party found by the address, else a person made from the sender's name), the project's triage assignee its Assignee. Each new or joined message is the request's: RequestEmailMessage, its CommunicationEvent (type Email) by RequestCommEvent, so Chatter shows it, and its files as RequestContent. The confirmation goes from the account when the form settings send one (not for a reply). Returns requestId and whether it was made.

parameter.name: value
parameter.description: The project (workEffortId), or empty for the plus tag

service.description: The createWorkItem action of the mail client's rules (EmailRuleAction ErActCreateWorkItem): a message from an internal sender (a user account with that address whose party is on the project) becomes a work item of the project (the action's value, or the plus tag's, as create#RequestFromEmail finds it): Task type, the subject its title, the text its description, the sender its owner and Reporter; its files and the message on the item (WorkEffortCommEvent). From anyone else, or with no project, it is a request (create#RequestFromEmail). A message already on a work item or request is left.

Internal, for the email rule actions: the project of a received message: the one value names (a workEffortId), else the one whose plus tag (WstIntakePlusTag) one of its To or Cc addresses carries (name+tag@...), preferring a project whose intake account is the message's. A project is given only when its intake account (WstIntakeAccount) is emailAccountId or the rule's owner (ruleOwnerUserId) holds a current role on it, so a rule cannot file mail into a project its owner has nothing to do with; a refused one is logged.

Internal: the organization a mail account works for, for the intake settings of a request with no project: the account owner's organization (an employee or member of an internal organization), else none.

Internal: the request a received message answers: one of the messages its In-Reply-To and References name (by Message-ID), its parent, or its thread's first message is on a request (RequestEmailMessage). Else none.

Internal: the party of a received message's sender: a person or organization, not disabled and not anyone's personal contact, with that email address in effect (a user account's party first); else a person made from the sender's name (Customer role; a name of one word, or none, has the address's domain as its last name) with the address. partyId and the address's contactMechId.

Internal: puts a received message on a request: RequestEmailMessage (with the sender's party), its CommunicationEvent (type Email, create#EmailCommunicationEvent) joined by RequestCommEvent so Chatter shows it, and its files (not the inline ones) copied as RequestContent. Each part on its own: one that fails is logged and the others go on.

Internal: the confirmation of a new request to its requester, from a project's intake account (emailAccountId; its default identity): "We received your request" with its number and subject, and that a reply adds to it. With parentEmailMessageId (the message that made it) it answers that message in its thread. The sent message is on the request (RequestEmailMessage), so a reply to it joins the request. Never fails: a send that does not go is logged and waits in the account's Outbox.
Internal, for the Request rule of entity/Request.eecas.xml: notify#RequestTriage after the commit of the change (at once when there is no transaction). A failure is logged, never the change's.

Tells the triagers of a request that it is new to them, on the topic RequestTriage: the project's triage assignee (WstTriageParty), else its managers (ProjectManager, Manager); for a request with no project, of a type Projects triages, the triage assignee of the organizations whose intake settings name one. Not the user who made the change. Run by the Request rule of entity/Request.eecas.xml (a request Submitted, or given a project); a failure is logged, not the request's. A request is told once for its project (a request made and given its project in one change runs this twice); force tells again.

A work item from a request (design-projects.md §6 MakeWorkItem): a task in the project (the request's when not given; a request with no project takes this one), linked by RequestWorkEffort, its title and description the request's unless given, its type from the request's (RqtBugFix a Bug Fix, RqtNewFeature a New Feature, else a Task), its priority and due the request's. A Submitted request becomes Reviewed (accepted) once it has work. The caller checks the user may add work to the project.

A request follows its work (design-projects.md §6 RequestDetail Actions), when the item is a project's and the project's setting WstRequestFromWork is Y, or is not set and the project has the Requests module (WstModules); a task with no project (Commons' tasks on a request) or a project outside Projects moves nothing, as in Mantle: when a linked work item (RequestWorkEffort, a task) starts (In Progress, In Review or In Testing) an open request not yet in progress moves to In Progress; when every linked item is done (Complete or Closed; a Cancelled one counts as neither, and at least one must be done) it moves to Completed with the resolution Fixed for a bug, else Completed. The followers of the request and its Reporter's and Assignee's users are told on the topic RequestUpdate. Run by the WorkEffort status rule of entity/Work.eecas.xml for the item whose status changed; each request on its own, a failure logged.

A request becomes a project's (design-projects.md §6 ConvertToProject): its project is set and it moves to In Progress. The caller made the project (NewProject or a quick project) and checks the user may.
